title: PracticePay Patient Financing: Limits on Open Plans per Customer and per Provider
content:
**Rule.** A customer may hold at most 3 PracticePay Patient Financing plans in approved or active status at the same time, and at one provider no more than the chosen plan's limit of open plans per provider. The customer holds fewer than the maximum number of open PracticePay plans, and fewer than the plan's per-provider limit at the chosen provider. Paid-off, cancelled, expired and declined plans do not count. Each new treatment needs its own plan.

## Condition for taking an application

An application for a new plan is taken only when, on Larkspur's own plan records for that customer, both of these hold before the application is registered:

| Check | Holds when |
|---|---|
| Plans held across all providers | the customer has fewer than 3 plans in approved or active status |
| Plans held at the chosen provider | the customer has fewer plans in approved or active status at that provider than the chosen plan's limit of open plans per provider (the per-plan figure in the entry-requirements schedule) |

The count is read from the system record of the customer's plans and their statuses and providers, not from what the customer says about them. Only approved and active plans are counted; a plan that is paid off, cancelled, expired or declined is left out of both counts.

## Worked cases (hypothetical customers)

- A customer with two active plans at two different providers applies at a third provider for a plan whose per-provider limit is 1: both counts are below their limits (2 is fewer than 3; 0 is fewer than 1), so the application is taken.
- A customer with three active plans applies for a fourth: 3 is not fewer than 3, so the application is not taken.
- A customer with one active plan at a provider applies there again for a plan whose per-provider limit is 1: 1 is not fewer than 1, so the application is not taken at that provider; for a plan whose per-provider limit is 2, it is taken.
- A customer whose earlier plan at the provider is paid off holds no counted plan there.
